title: Unified Inference: Product overview, PRD, design specs, roadmap & pricing (Q1-Q3 2026)
author: Mariana Lopez
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the Product Overview, PRD-level requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference initiative (hosted + dedicated + private runtimes). The goal is to provide a single, reviewable reference for engineering, product, sales, and go-to-market teams ahead of the Q2 2026 rollout.

1) Summary and context
- Problem: Customers require a single inference API and operational model that provides predictable latency, cost control, and consistent behavior across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Outcomes: A unified product surface that simplifies developer adoption, reduces integration friction, and enables cost/latency tradeoffs via clear controls (batching, quantization profiles, routing policies).

2) Product goals (OKRs mapped)
- O1: Reduce time-to-first-response for new developers by 30% (Q2 2026).
- O2: Deliver documented cost controls that reduce per-token cost by >= 15% for sample e-commerce and chat workloads (Q3 2026).
- O3: Achieve parity of core API and observability across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments by GA.

3) Scope (in & out)
In-scope:
- Single REST/SDK surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking.
- Model catalog with curated performance/quantization profiles and compatibility matrix.
- Batch and cache controls surfaced in API + console.
- Per-route dashboards and rollout tools (canary + A/B).

Out-of-scope (for this release):
- Custom on-prem hardware connectors (planned for Private v2).
- Enterprise billing integrations beyond standard invoicing.

4) Key success metrics
- Developer activation: API key to first successful request < 10 minutes (measured via quickstart funnel).
- Cost efficiency: mean tokens per dollar improvement >= 15% on target workloads.
- Reliability: 99.9% availability for hosted model invocations (SLA targets for dedicated contracts).
- Observability adoption: >70% of new customers enable per-route latency/cost dashboards within 30 days.

5) Requirements (functional & non-functional)
Functional requirements (priority)
| id | requirement | acceptance criteria | owner |
|----|-------------|---------------------|-------|
| FR-001 | Unified inference API | Single REST/SDK routes for text, chat, embeddings. SDK examples for Python/Node. | Product/SDK |
| FR-002 | Model catalog + compatibility matrix | Catalog lists verified models, quant profiles, and hardware compatibility. | Product/Research |
| FR-003 | Cost/latency controls | API flags for batching, quant-profile hints, and route-level routing policy. | Product/Runtime |
| FR-004 | Observability per-route | Dashboards exposing tokens, latency P50/P95/P99, and cost breakdown. | Platform/Observability |

Non-functional requirements
- NFR-001: 99.9% uptime for hosted endpoints (excluding scheduled maintenance).
- NFR-002: P95 latency targets documented per model/sequence-length (see perf table below).
- NFR-003: Data residency and encryption: support region pinning and KMS integrations for Private deployments.

6) Performance and sizing table (example SLOs)
| model | sequence len | target P95 latency (ms) | recommended deployment |
|-------|--------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| redwood/gptx-13b | 512 | 220 | hosted/dedicated (A100) |
| open/llama-70b | 1024 | 850 | dedicated (H100) |
| redwood/embedding-2 | 256 | 35 | hosted |

7) High-level design and implementation notes
- Architecture overview:
  - Control plane: unified API gateway routes requests to runtime clusters by routing policy (latency/cost/region).
  - Runtime clusters: model-optimized fleets (quantization-aware) with continuous batching and prefix cache layers.
  - Observability: token-level tracing collector that tags requests with route, model, quant-profile, and customer_id.

- Design decisions (short)
  1) Single API design (v1) with granular flags rather than multiple separated endpoints to reduce cognitive load.
  2) Model variants surfaced through the catalog, not as separate endpoints, to enable dynamic fallback.
  3) Routing policies implemented in control plane to allow policy updates without tenant code changes.

- Security & compliance notes:
  - Private deployments will default to customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.
  - Audit logging required for model serving actions (model loads, rollouts, policy changes).

8) API contract (examples)
- Text generation (POST /v1/generate)
  Request body (JSON example):
  {
    "model": "redwood/gptx-13b",
    "input": "Summarize the following product brief...",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "batching": { "priority": "latency", "max_batch_delay_ms": 8 },
    "quant_profile": "int8-balanced"
  }

  Response: streaming chunks with token and meta headers for model_variant and cost_estimate.

9) Design specs: modules & ownership
- Runtime kernel selection (eng-serving-runtime)
  - Owners: Kernel team; deliverable: kernel selector v1 with heuristics for sequence length and quant-profile.
- Control plane routing & policy (eng-platform)
  - Owners: Routing team; deliverable: policy engine with canary rollout support.
- Observability + Console (eng-platform + eng-developer-experience)
  - Owners: Console team; deliverable: per-route dashboards and tracing integration.

10) Roadmap & themes (Q1-Q3 2026)
- Q1 2026 (design & early experiments):
  - Model catalog prototype and quant-profile registry.
  - API contract draft and SDK examples.
  - Pilot with two customers on Dedicated.
- Q2 2026 (beta):
  - GA of unified REST/SDK for hosted with core observability.
  - Console per-route dashboards and basic rollout tooling.
  - Pricing pilot for Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Q3 2026 (GA & enterprise):
  - Private deployment GA with KMS integration and audit logging.
  - Billing-packaging finalized and marketplace listing.

Themes: "Developer-first onboarding", "Predictable economics", "Unified operations".

11) Pricing & packaging notes (guiding principles)
- Principles:
  1) Simple entry: keep hosted per-token pricing understandable for PLG motion.
  2) Predictable scale: offer Reserved/Dedicated pricing with committed throughput and burst allowances.
  3) Workload-aware add-ons: advanced observability retention, extended SLAs, and private deployment packaging.

- Proposed pricing tiers (summary table):
| tier | target customer | billing model | highlights |
|------|-----------------|---------------|-----------|
| Self-serve Hosted | startups, devs | usage (per-token + embedding unit) | free tier + pay-as-you-go |
| Dedicated | mid-market, scale-ups | committed monthly capacity + overage | SLA-backed latency, burst option |
| Private | enterprise | licensing + deployment fee + support | KMS, audit, region isolation |

- Packaging notes:
  - Dedicated contracts to include a baseline throughput, defined model families, and optional reserved model variants for lower latency.
  - Marketplace listing to bundle Private deployment with onboarding and security package.

12) Release notes (latest changes - 2026-02-25)
- New features:
  - GA-ready unified /v1/generate API (beta previously) with batching controls and quant_profile hints.
  - Model catalog v0.9 with compatibility flags and recommended deployment types.
  - Per-route console dashboard (beta) with token-level cost breakdown.
- Bug fixes and improvements:
  - Reduced cold-start latency for cached prefix loads by 18% on A100 fleets.
  - Fixed race condition in rollout policy evaluation under high-concurrency.

13) Rollout checklist and runbook (short)
1. Documentation published and linked (this page).
2. SDKs updated (Python/Node) and smoke-tested.
3. Internal GA announcement and support FAQ prepared.
4. Pilot customers migrated to new API in canary mode for two weeks.
5. Monitor key metrics (activation time, P95 latency, tokens per dollar) for 14 days post-rollout.

14) Risks and mitigations
- Risk: Early model variants produce unacceptable quality regressions when using quantized profiles.
  Mitigation: Auto-fallback to higher-fidelity model variant + require canary evaluation against labeled prompt sets.
- Risk: Customers misunderstand pricing tradeoffs and enable aggressive batching that increases tail latency.
  Mitigation: Console warnings, default conservative batching settings, and per-route guardrails.

15) Ownership and next steps
- Product owner: Mariana Lopez (mariana@redwood.ai)
- Engineering leads: Evan Kim (runtime), Priya Shah (console), Alex Rivera (platform)
Next steps:

Appendix: Example evaluation checklist for quant profiles
1. Define prompt set (50 prompts) representative of target workload.
2. Run baseline (no quant) to collect quality metrics.
3. Run quantized variant and compare BLEU/ROUGE/LLR-like metrics plus human-review on top 10 failures.
4. Approve profile only if quality degradation <= 3% and latency improvement >= 12%.
